test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The accuracy of the dial bore gauge instrument depends on which of the following parts?

options.text: A pointer on a graduated dial
A dot indicator on a linear scale
A marking on a logarithmic dial
An arrow on a semi-circular scale

solution:
The correct answer is __A pointer on a graduated dial.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• A pointer on a graduated dial__ is a critical part of a dial bore gauge instrument.
 
• The graduated dial helps in accurately measuring the internal dimensions of a bore.
 
• It indicates changes in dimension with high precision and clarity.
 
• Any misalignment or error in the pointer can affect measurement accuracy.
 
• Dial bore gauges are widely used in engineering applications to ensure tight tolerances and quality control.
 
• They are essential in industries such as automotive and aerospace manufacturing.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Dot Indicator on a Linear Scale:**

 
 
• This is not typically used in dial bore gauges, as linear scales are more common in calipers.
 
• It is less suitable for circular or bore measurements.
 
 
 
• **Marking on a Logarithmic Dial:**
 
 
• Logarithmic dials are used in specialized instruments, not in standard dial bore gauges.
 
• They are designed for applications where changes follow a logarithmic scale.
 
 
 
• **Arrow on a Semi-Circular Scale:**
 
 
• Semi-circular scales are less precise compared to graduated dials.
 
• They are not typically used for internal bore measurements.
